platform: Linux x86-64; local glibc 2.36, release floor 2.38.
observations: Both archives were built from freshly compiled ordinary Lean source: automatic API discovery first, then an independently compiled source package checked against the reviewed API. Both produced the same Binding IR; their component identities differ.

The installer verified the package-set receipts, source tree hashes, complete archive inventories and loader paths. Two independent clients, compiled via pkg-config and CMake, ran with relocated packages, no producer sources and PATH=/nonexistent.

All 19 copied primitive callback arguments and replies ran on the main thread, including a 4096-bit GMP integer, a Unicode scalar, embedded NUL, binary octets, fixed-width boundaries, negative zero and infinity.

A callback ran during factory construction, in a worker task and again after factory return. A callback drove a second installed component; driving its own task returned BUSY. Waiting used one borrowed descriptor with no reads or timers in the consumer.

Releasing the last public callback handle did not revoke the task's private reference. Explicit self-close allowed the active call to return and prevented the next call. Stale, mismatched-signature, foreign-component, forked and off-thread uses did not enter the host. Queued cancellation and late-created inner task cancellation did not invoke the disposed context.

Escaping C failures preserved code and payload identity; the owner disposed that payload exactly once. Caught failures produced returned Except data; equal-message replacement produced terminal Lean IO. Eager/factory IO, terminal IO, typed EIO, invalid UTF-8, negative Nat and over-budget replies remained distinct.

A cooperative parked task in a different component became readable when an explicit trap, unrecognized callback status, self-cancel-then-trap or external retirement poisoned the shared runtime. It settled UNAVAILABLE with its output unchanged. Normal and isolated runs returned to zero live identities and the baseline descriptor count.

runtimeCoexistence.outcome: The same executable loaded with either original broker first. The new runtime ran tasks from both generations. The old runtime ran completion-only operations and rejected a retained start with UNAVAILABLE before invoking the host.

scope: Local installed C11 evidence for copied primitive unary callbacks retained by actual Lean tasks on Linux x86-64. This does not establish resource-bearing callback replies, arbitrary foreign threads, signal/longjmp recovery, other targets, hosted CI or registry publication.
